pr_title: Add a workaround for unbinding script members on Mono
pr_comments:
> I would expect something like this to work on both .NET and Mono:

Unfortunately it's not as simple to index a dictionary like this.

```
foreach (var key in members.Keys)
	if (targetType == members[key].Target.GetType())
		members.Remove(key);
```
came to mind as well, but I fear we'll run into the same problem, just with modifying the `KeyCollection` this time.

comments:
This seems to be a mono bug.

The code in question is [here](https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/blob/a2a34dafdec5c10c233fa65cd52e5519e6d1b1f3/OpenRA.Game/Scripting/ScriptObjectWrapper.cs#L66-L68).

```
protected void Unbind(Type targetType)
{
	foreach (var m in members)
		if (targetType == m.Value.Target.GetType())
			members.Remove(m.Key);
}
```

This is totally fine in netcore 3.0+, as mutating a dictionary using the `Remove` or `Clear` methods during enumeration is fine:

>An enumerator remains valid as long as the collection remains unchanged. If changes are made to the collection, such as adding elements or changing the capacity, the enumerator is irrecoverably invalidated and the next call to [MoveNext](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.dictionary-2.enumerator.movenext?view=net-6.0) or [IEnumerator.Reset](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.dictionary-2.enumerator.system-collections-ienumerator-reset?view=net-6.0) throws an [InvalidOperationException](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.invalidoperationexception?view=net-6.0).
>
>**.NET Core 3.0+ only: The only mutating methods which do not invalidate enumerators are [Remove](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.dictionary-2.remove?view=net-6.0) and [Clear](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.dictionary-2.clear?view=net-6.0).**

[Source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.dictionary-2.getenumerator?view=net-6.0#remarks) (emphasis mine).

It would appear that mono doesn't implement this behaviour, however.

I tried modifying the code to avoid modifying the dictionary during enumeration. Unfortunately there doesn't seem to be any great way to do this without creating another temporary collection of KVPs or key strings. Mono's stop-the-world garbage collection doesn't really put up with this very well however, and game performance seems to degrade over time.

Looks like I'm incorrect to call this a mono bug, as mono is intended to track .NET framework, not .NET core. Removing the dependency on mono for unix-like systems would likely be ideal.

https://stackoverflow.com/a/58618694/203705

> Here's the modified `Unbind` that avoids the issue, but introduces too much object churn IMO to be useful under mono.

I propose #20356 which disables this code path for our default .NET 6 builds, and re-uses the `toRemove` list to save some performance.

Interesting. I was aware when implementing and read in the docs it had to be save from a certain .net version. Later Roosterdragon made a remark about it. 

How does it relate to the crash info mentioning it uses mono 6? Yet in the source you check for mono 5 or greater?
